title: Warm Starting Neural Dynamics Models From Few Jacobian Samples
abstract: arXiv:2611.21465v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) leverages a model of the environment, used for planning and generating samples without interacting with the real world. Motivated by evidence that informed initialization significantly improves the efficiency of MBRL, we propose TDec-Init, an algorithm to warm-start neural dynamics models using transition Jacobians. Using a decoupling algorithm based on the decomposition of a tensor of stacked Jacobian samples, we recover weights and flexible nonlinearities, and use them to initialize a feedforward neural network. In the low-data regime, we show on several benchmark environments that our approach outperforms random initialization and value training, and either matches or outperforms Sobolev training, while requiring fewer training steps between episodes.

translated_title: 从少量雅可比样本热启动神经动力学模型
translated_abstract: 基于模型的强化学习（MBRL）利用环境模型进行规划，并在不与真实世界交互的情况下生成样本。鉴于有证据表明有依据的初始化能显著提高MBRL的效率，我们提出了TDec-Init，这是一种利用转移雅可比矩阵对神经动力学模型进行热启动的算法。通过一种基于堆叠雅可比样本张量分解的解耦算法，我们恢复了权重和灵活的非线性函数，并用它们来初始化前馈神经网络。在低数据场景下，我们在多个基准环境中展示了我们的方法优于随机初始化和价值训练，并且匹配或超越了Sobolev训练，同时在回合之间需要更少的训练步数。
tldr: 本文提出TDec-Init算法，通过分解少量堆叠的转移雅可比样本张量来恢复权重和非线性以热启动神经动力学模型，在低数据场景下性能优于随机初始化和价值训练，且匹配或超越Sobolev训练，同时减少回合间的训练步数。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes TDec-Init, an algorithm that warm-starts neural dynamics models by decomposing stacked transition Jacobian samples to recover weights and nonlinearities, outperforming random initialization and value training while matching or exceeding Sobolev training in low-data regimes with fewer training steps between episodes.
